title: Zubrytsya
summary: Zubrytsia is a village located in the Drohobych Raion of Lviv Oblast, Ukraine, known for its historical significance and local architecture.

sections.heading: Geographical Context
paragraphs: Zubrytsia ([[ukrainian|Ukrainian]]: Зубриця, Polish: Zubrzyca) is situated in the south-western part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]], specifically within [[drohobych|Drohobych]] Raion, [[lviv-oblast|Lviv Oblast]].

sections.heading: Administrative Structure
paragraphs: The village is part of the Skhidnytsia settlement hromada, which is one of the hromadas [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

Prior to 18 July 2020, Zubrytsia was part of Turka Raion, which was dissolved as a result of the administrative reform in Ukraine that aimed to streamline the number of raions in Lviv Oblast to seven.

sections.heading: Historical Development
paragraphs: Originally, Zubrytsia started as a hamlet of Holovske and gained independence in the late 19th century.

sections.heading: Cultural Heritage
paragraphs: The village is notable for its Orthodox church, which was constructed in 1871, reflecting the local architectural and cultural heritage.
